title: unified-lts-support-coverage-and-safety-harness
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design and deliver a single source LTS support coverage and upgrade safety harness that specifies which runtime, API, SDK, and console versions are included in each LTS lane, defines automated rollout gates, and provides upgrade automation to reduce customer outage risk.
background: We currently have fragmented LTS guidance across runtime, API, SDKs, and console. Customers and sales are confused about what is guaranteed in an LTS lane, and engineering teams lack a canonical dataset for making compatibility and rollback decisions. This ticket consolidates policy and builds the safety tooling to enforce it.
decision_summary: Adopt a three-lane LTS model: Stability (24-month supported), Maintenance (12-month security-only), and Current (6-month compatibility overlap). Each lane will include a compatibility matrix with minimum/maximum supported versions per surface, automated preflight checks, and gating rules encoded in the release pipeline. Backwards-incompatible APIs require explicit deprecation windows and opt-in feature flags during overlap period.
compatibility_matrix:
Format: CSV-style table encoded in docs and as a JSON manifest for tooling. Example rows:
- runtime: 1.18.x (Stability), 1.19.x (Maintenance), 1.20.x (Current)
- api: v1 (Stability), v1.1 (Maintenance), v2 (Current, feature-flag opt-in)
- sdk-js: 2.5.x (Stability), 2.6.x (Maintenance), 3.0.x (Current)
- console: 2025.12 (Stability), 2026.02 (Maintenance), 2026.04 (Current)
Each matrix entry includes: supported=true/false, minimum_patch, rollback_test_id (link to smoke test dashboard). The canonical matrix will live at: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/redwood-release/docs/lts-matrix.csv and an authoritative JSON at https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-manifests/pulls/487
rollout_gates:
Gates to enforce before promoting to an LTS lane: 
1) Telemetry pass (no >1% error regressions across 7-day baseline)
2) Regression-free model responses (evaluations on 5 curated prompts)
3) End-to-end smoke tests (runtime+api+sdk+console) green for 48h
4) Automated backward-compatibility verifier runs (consumer contracts)
5) Manual security review for changes touching auth/KMS.
Gate implementation: scripted checks in CI that post gate artifacts to the release dashboard and block promotion when failing.
upgrade_tooling:
Implement 'lts-upgrade-check' CLI that:
- Downloads canonical manifest
- Runs API/SDK compatibility harness against staged infra
- Validates migration scripts and DB-key compatibility where applicable
- Produces a deterministic migration/rollback plan (patch-level)
- Integrates with release orchestration: GitHub Actions + internal deployer.
Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/lts-upgrade-check (PRs: #102, #110)
migration_steps: 1) Publish canonical LTS manifest and version pins. 2) Integrate manifest into release pipelines for runtime, api, sdk, and console builds. 3) Add preflight checks to canary jobs. 4) Run an initial cross-surface rehearsal targeting internal staging customers. 5) Iterate on gating thresholds after observation window. 6) Announce deprecation windows to customers and update docs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Canonical LTS manifest committed and referenced by release pipelines.
- 'lts-upgrade-check' exits non-zero on a deliberately broken compat scenario (unit tests).
- Release dashboard shows gate statuses and links to failing artifacts.
- At least one cross-surface staged promotion completed with all gates passing and no remediation required.
- Product and Security have reviewed and signed off on the policy doc.
